units.text: If your driver license or driving privilege is revoked, it means your license has been canceled.
units.reason: The context states that revocation means your license has been canceled.

units.text: You must reapply for a new license after the revocation period ends.
units.reason: The context says you must reapply for a new license after the revocation period ends.

units.text: In most cases, you must first request DMV approval before obtaining a new license.
units.reason: The context states that in most cases you must first request DMV approval before obtaining a new license.

units.text: You may need to retake the written and road tests and pay a license reapplication fee.
units.reason: The context says you may need to retake written and road tests and pay a reapplication fee.

units.text: Your application may be denied if you have a high-risk driving record or fail to meet DMV requirements.
units.reason: The context states that your application may be denied if you have a high-risk driving record or fail to meet DMV requirements.

units.text: You may also need to pay a driver civil penalty before your license or driving privilege is restored.
units.reason: The context says you may need to pay a driver civil penalty before restoration.

units.text: If your revocation was due to an uninsured accident, you must contact the DMV Insurance Services Bureau.
units.reason: The context states that if revocation is due to an uninsured accident, you must contact the DMV Insurance Services Bureau.

units.text: Paying the civil penalty does not restore your driving privilege; you must apply and be approved by DMV.
units.reason: The context states that paying the civil penalty does not restore driving privilege; you must apply and be approved by DMV.
